\chapter{Asking the Way}
\label{ch:ur-asking-the-way}
\hlchaptermodality{270}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask the way and how far it is (isṭeshan kaise jāte haiṅ? kitnī dūr hai?), and ask or tell someone politely (bāeṅ muṛiye, zarā batāiye).}

Complete UR-R270-asking-the-way: ask the way, and ask or tell politely.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کتنا} (kitnā)}{کتنا (kitnā)}]{\ur{کتنا} (kitnā) — how much, how many}

\label{lesson:UR-C270-kitna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say \textquotedblleft{}a fare\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}far\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{kirāyā}, \emph{dūr}.) A traveller asks about both.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کتنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کتنا}} — \emph{kitnā} — \textquotedblleft{}how much; how many\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{کرایہ} \ur{کتنا} \ur{ہے؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kirāyā kitnā hai?} — \textquotedblleft{}How much is the fare?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

It follows its noun like \textbf{\ur{اچھا}} (\emph{achchhā}): \textbf{\ur{کتنا}} for \textbf{\ur{کرایہ}}, \textbf{\ur{کتنے}} (\emph{kitne}) for a plural.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{کتنے} \ur{مسافر} \ur{تھے؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kitne musāfir the?} — \textquotedblleft{}How many passengers were there?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{کتنی} \ur{دور}} (\emph{kitnī dūr}), \textquotedblleft{}how far\textquotedblright{}, goes as one pair:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{اسٹیشن} \ur{کتنی} \ur{دور} \ur{ہے؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{isṭeshan kitnī dūr hai?} — \textquotedblleft{}How far is the station?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کتنا}} (\emph{kitnā}) is inherited. CDIAL lists its Hindi twin, with the sense \textquotedblleft{}how great?\textquotedblright{}, under a reconstructed \emph{kiyatta} (CDIAL 3167).
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kitnā}, then \emph{kirāyā kitnā hai?}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}How far is the market?\textquotedblright{} — \emph{bāzār kitnī dūr hai?}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\ur{کتنا}} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}How much, how many\textquotedblright{}.) \textquotedblleft{}How far is the station?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ur{اسٹیشن} \ur{کتنی} \ur{دور} \ur{ہے؟}})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ذرا} (zarā)}{ذرا (zarā)}]{\ur{ذرا} (zarā) — a little}

\label{lesson:UR-C270-zara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say \textquotedblleft{}how much is the fare?\textquotedblright{} (\emph{kirāyā kitnā hai?}) Then \textquotedblleft{}expensive\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{mahãgā}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ذرا}}
\textbf{\ur{ذرا}} — \emph{zarā} — \textquotedblleft{}a little\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{ذرا} \ur{مہنگا} \ur{ہے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih zarā mahãgā hai.} — \textquotedblleft{}This is a little expensive.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{ذرا} \ur{آرام} \ur{سے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zarā ārām se.} — \textquotedblleft{}A little more slowly, please.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Before a request it softens it, as \textquotedblleft{}please\textquotedblright{} does. The next lessons put it to work.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ذرا}} (\emph{zarā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{dharra}, \textquotedblleft{}a speck, an atom\textquotedblright{}. Its first letter is new to your hand; the next lesson takes it out.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{zarā}, then \emph{zarā ārām se}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}This is a little difficult\textquotedblright{} — \emph{yih zarā mushkil hai}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\ur{ذرا}} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A little\textquotedblright{}.) What does it do before a request? (It softens it.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ذ} (zāl)}{ذ (zāl)}]{\ur{ذ} (zāl) — the letter that opens \ur{ذرا}}

\label{lesson:UR-W270-zal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ur{غ} once, and name it. (\emph{ghain}.)

Now say \textbf{\ur{ذرا}} (\emph{zarā}), \textquotedblleft{}a little\textquotedblright{}. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ur{ذ}}
\textbf{\ur{ذ}} — \emph{zāl}, the sound \emph{z}.

It opens \textbf{\ur{ذرا}} (\emph{zarā}). You already write \textbf{\ur{د}}: \textbf{\ur{ذ}} is that shape with \textbf{one dot} above it. Like \textbf{\ur{د}}, it does not join the letter after it. It is one more way Urdu writes \emph{z}, beside \textbf{\ur{ز}}, \textbf{\ur{ض}} and \textbf{\ur{ظ}}, and it comes in words from Arabic.

\subsection*{Writing: \ur{ذ}}
Put your pen on \ur{ذ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ur{ذرا}} and point at \ur{ذ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ur{ذ} three times, saying \emph{z} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\ur{ذرا}} once, with the dot above its first letter
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ur{ذرا}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ur{ذ}? (\textbf{zāl}, \emph{z}.) What tells it from \ur{د}? (The dot.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ur{ذرا}}, \emph{zarā}, \textquotedblleft{}a little\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کیسے} \ur{جاتے} \ur{ہیں} (kaise jāte haiṅ)}{کیسے جاتے ہیں (kaise jāte haiṅ)}]{\ur{کیسے} \ur{جاتے} \ur{ہیں} (kaise jāte haiṅ) — asking the way}

\label{lesson:UR-C270-kaise-jate-hain}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}where?\textquotedblright{} (\emph{kahāṅ?}) Then \textquotedblleft{}how far is the station?\textquotedblright{} (\emph{isṭeshan kitnī dūr hai?}) Now ask the way there.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: how do you get there?}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{اسٹیشن} \ur{کہاں} \ur{ہے؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{isṭeshan kahāṅ hai?} — \textquotedblleft{}Where is the station?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{اسٹیشن} \ur{کیسے} \ur{جاتے} \ur{ہیں؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{isṭeshan kaise jāte haiṅ?} — \textquotedblleft{}How do you get to the station?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Word for word, \textquotedblleft{}how do people go to the station?\textquotedblright{}: the plural \textbf{\ur{جاتے} \ur{ہیں}} (\emph{jāte haiṅ}) asks about anyone.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{کیا} \ur{راستہ} \ur{لمبا} \ur{ہے؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kyā rāstā lambā hai?} — \textquotedblleft{}Is it a long way?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: the polite request}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{سیدھے} \ur{جائیے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sīdhe jāiye.} — \textquotedblleft{}Go straight on.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{جائیے}} (\emph{jāiye}) is \textbf{\ur{جانا}} asked of someone you call \textbf{\ur{آپ}}. The stem takes \textbf{-\ur{یے}} (\emph{-iye}); after a vowel, \textbf{-\ur{ئیے}}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{بائیں} \ur{مڑیے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāeṅ muṛiye.} — \textquotedblleft{}Turn left.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{پل} \ur{کے} \ur{بعد} \ur{دائیں} \ur{مڑیے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pul ke bād dāeṅ muṛiye.} — \textquotedblleft{}After the bridge, turn right.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{ذرا} \ur{بتائیے،} \ur{بازار} \ur{کہاں} \ur{ہے؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zarā batāiye, bāzār kahāṅ hai?} — \textquotedblleft{}Could you tell me where the market is?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{سنیے}} (\emph{suniye}), \textquotedblleft{}listen\textquotedblright{}, opens a question to a stranger: \textquotedblleft{}excuse me\textquotedblright{}. A few verbs bend the stem, among them \textbf{\ur{دیجیے}} (\emph{dījiye}) from \textbf{\ur{دینا}}, \textbf{\ur{لیجیے}} (\emph{lījiye}) from \textbf{\ur{لینا}}, \textbf{\ur{کیجیے}} (\emph{kījiye}) from \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Turn left\textquotedblright{} — \emph{bāeṅ muṛiye}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Turn right\textquotedblright{} — \emph{dāeṅ muṛiye}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Go straight on\textquotedblright{} — \emph{sīdhe jāiye}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}How do you get to the market?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ur{بازار} \ur{کیسے} \ur{جاتے} \ur{ہیں؟}}) \textquotedblleft{}Turn right\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{دائیں} \ur{مڑیے}}.) \textquotedblleft{}Please tell me\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{ذرا} \ur{بتائیے}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — asking the way}

\label{lesson:UR-R270-asking-the-way}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}you should go\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}so I didn't come\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{āp ko jānā chāhiye}, \emph{is liye maiṅ nahīṅ āyā}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} Excuse me, how do you get to the station?
  \item \emph{Say it:} How far is it? How much is the fare?
  \item \emph{Say it:} Go straight on, then turn left after the bridge.
  \item \emph{Say it:} Could you tell me where the market is?
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\ur{ذرا}} once, and point at \ur{ذ} inside it
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}How many passengers?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ur{کتنے} \ur{مسافر؟}}) Now the other way round: from \textbf{\ur{مڑیے}}, what is the verb? (\textbf{\ur{مڑنا}}.) The polite form of \textbf{\ur{دینا}}? (\textbf{\ur{دیجیے}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
